page.metaDescription: Track government publications, grant announcements, regulatory portals, and inter-agency policy changes. Built for public-sector and government-affairs teams.
page.h1: Website monitoring for government and public-sector teams
page.subtitle: Track agency publications, grant announcements, inter-agency policy updates, and statutory changes from one consolidated dashboard.
page.intro: Government affairs, public-sector consultants, and inter-agency coordination teams need awareness across dozens of federal and state agencies. WebMonitor.fyi automates the portal-polling layer across Federal Register, Regulations.gov, agency rule pages, grants.gov, state portals, and international equivalents. Built for lobbyists, government affairs professionals at corporations and nonprofits, grant-seeking research institutions, and policy analysts.

challenges.title: Inter-agency policy coordination
challenges.body: A single policy issue often spans multiple agencies — EPA, DOE, USDA for environmental; SEC, FDIC, OCC for finance. Centralized monitoring keeps everything in one place.

challenges.title: Grant and funding opportunity tracking
challenges.body: NIH, NSF, DOE, state-level grant portals all publish on their own cadences. Grant-seekers monitoring opportunity announcements catch them before the deadline window closes.

challenges.title: State-level coverage
challenges.body: Multi-state operators (cannabis, gaming, transportation) face 50 different regulatory environments. Monitors on the highest-priority state portals — swapped as the rulemaking calendar moves — make state-level tracking tractable.

challenges.title: Comment period and docket monitoring
challenges.body: Regulations.gov dockets accept comments on rolling windows. Government-affairs teams watch for docket activity to time their filings and assess opposition.

page.limits: WebMonitor reads the public-facing surface — Federal Register, Regulations.gov, agency rule pages, grants.gov, state portals. Pre-decisional drafts circulated inside an agency, FACA committee non-public materials, and FOIA-pending content aren't monitorable until they post publicly. State portals also vary in stability; some change URL structures during redesigns and need the monitor URL updated.

faq.q: Can I track grants.gov for new opportunity announcements?
faq.a: Yes. The grants.gov search results page works as a monitor URL. Filter by CFDA number or keyword to narrow to relevant opportunities.

faq.q: Does this work for international regulators?
faq.a: Yes. EU Official Journal, gov.uk consultations, Canadian Gazette, Australian regulator portals — anything publicly accessible by URL works.

faq.q: Can a state-level government-affairs team monitor across all 50 states?
faq.a: Not all at once — plans include up to five monitors. Teams typically point them at the states with active rulemaking or pending applications and update the monitor URLs as the calendar moves.

faq.q: How does this compare to Politico Pro or Bloomberg Government?
faq.a: Those platforms include editorial coverage and analyst dashboards. WebMonitor is the underlying alert layer — typically used alongside them rather than instead of them.
